_comment: Recruitable allies (bible section 6, roadmap v0.0.9). They level with the player via level_offset and fight themselves through the AI registry in engine/combat/ai.py. Any with marriageable:true can be married on the same terms as townspeople (section 15) - gender is never considered.

companions.name: Rook
companions.description: A retired sellsword who stayed in Ashvale because leaving cost more than staying.
dialogue: Stay behind me and this stays simple.
I've buried better fighters than either of us. Keep your guard up.
You swing like you're angry. Anger's fine. Sloppy isn't.
Quiet roads make me nervous. Loud ones make me useful.
I once guarded a duke's hat for three days. The duke was elsewhere.
Soup is tactics. Bad soup ruins morale before the enemy gets a chance.
Ashvale's well owes me money. Long story.

companions.name: Sister Elen
companions.description: Left the shrine when it stopped answering questions. Still keeps the vows that mattered.
dialogue: You're hurt. Sit. That wasn't a request.
The shrine taught mercy. The road taught triage.
I can keep you standing. I can't keep you sensible.
Every prayer I know is just a very old instruction. They still work.
I collect terrible jokes. They remind patients to keep breathing.
Half my family prays before meals. The other half checks for poison.
Voss tried to label my medicine cabinet. He has recovered.

companions.name: Kess
companions.description: Fast, cheerful, and entirely unbothered by the word 'ambush'.
dialogue: Found you a shortcut. It's only a bit haunted.
Rook says I'm reckless. Rook is slow. Draw your own conclusions.
If it bleeds, it has a schedule. I just move it up.
Don't look behind us. Actually - do, and then run.
I named my left boot. The right one hasn't earned it.
Beastkin ears are excellent. Yours are very loud, somehow.
If this plan works, I invented it. If not, Rook did.

companions.name: Magister Voss
companions.description: Studies the Sunken Shrine because nobody sensible will. Glass, but the sharp kind.
dialogue: The shrine is older than the language on it. Doesn't that trouble you?
Stand clear of the target. I mean genuinely clear.
I have three theories. Two of them end badly for us.
Knowledge first, safety somewhere after. It's a working order.
I am not banned from the archive. The archive is banned from me.
Elven patience is real. I simply spend mine quickly.
A wisp followed me home once. We disagreed about rent.

companions.name: Captain Brann
companions.description: Emberwatch's captain, off duty only by technicality.
dialogue: A wall is just a promise made from stone.
The western road burns because nobody has convinced it to stop.
Stand your watch. Even when nobody thanks you.
Ash gets into everything. Discipline keeps it out of the important parts.
Dwarven tea should hold a spoon upright. Anything weaker is weather.
My beard caught fire once. The recruits learned faster afterward.
Walls listen better than officers and interrupt less.

companions.name: Nyra Reed
companions.description: A marsh guide who can identify danger by how quiet the frogs become.
dialogue: If the reeds stop moving, you should too.
Maps are apologies for not knowing the ground.
The marsh isn't cruel. Cruelty requires interest.
Follow exactly. Heroics sink faster than boots.
My elven side reads the stars. My human side asks where supper is.
Never trust a frog with nothing to say.
I have six maps of this marsh. At most two are lying.

companions.name: Orren Quill
companions.description: Stonehaven's runesmith keeps testing inscriptions on live problems.
dialogue: A rune is an argument reality has agreed to lose.
Do not touch the blue chisel.
The crystals sing. Mostly complaints.
If this explodes, remember the pattern. The pattern is valuable.
The horns are useful for hanging measuring string. Dignity adapts.
I wrote a rune for silence. Tala smashed it for being suspiciously quiet.
Tea tastes better from a beaker. This is not negotiable.

companions.name: Tala Stone
companions.description: A forewoman who negotiates with cave-ins using an axe.
dialogue: Rock talks. Usually right before it falls.
Nobody is trapped until I say the tunnel is closed.
A bigger hammer is a kind of planning.
Stonehaven stands because we keep putting it back.
My axe is called Delicate Negotiation.
I can sing mining songs or sing well. Pick one.
Orren says crystals remember insults. Good. Saves me repeating them.

companions.name: Seraphine Gale
companions.description: A weather scholar whose forecasts occasionally fight beside her.
dialogue: The forecast says pain with scattered thunder.
Clouds are just rivers nobody can stand in.
Count after the flash. If you reach three, it wasn't mine.
Skyreach teaches perspective and very secure knots.
Demons invented contracts because handshakes kept setting things on fire.
I asked the cloud its name. It rained on me for an hour.
My forecast for supper is bread with a strong chance of cheese.

companions.name: Cael Sunward
companions.description: The last ruin guide willing to cross the Obsidian Gate twice.
dialogue: The gate opens for confidence. It closes for arrogance.
Morning is beautiful from up here. Dangerous, but beautiful.
The ruins remember footsteps. Walk like you want to be remembered kindly.
I've crossed twice. The third time should be almost sensible.
Dragonkin shed scales. No, you may not sell mine.
I polish my sword when nervous. It has become extremely shiny.
The Tyrant called me hatchling. Technically correct. Still rude.

companions.name: Lethira Vale
companions.description: An elven pathkeeper whose missing memories have begun growing as silver leaves.
dialogue: This path remembers me, though I do not remember it.
Silver leaves only grow where a promise was forgotten.
Do not step on that root. It holds grudges.
I have lived two hundred years and still burn porridge.
Your footsteps are easy to recognise. They sound determined and slightly lost.
Kess once challenged me to a race. I let the story improve in the retelling.
If I recover every memory, I hope at least one explains this hat.
The forest is not silent. It is choosing whether to include us.

companions.name: Brokk Embervein
companions.description: A dwarven resonance-smith who hears a missing clan verse beneath Stonehaven.
dialogue: The deep song has a missing note. My clan has a missing name.
A proper rune is carved once and argued over forever.
Never drink from a cup that hums.
My grandmother could split granite with a look. Grandfather was very polite.
Surface rain is just a cave leak with ambitions.
Tala swings first. I make sure the ceiling agrees.
I baked this bread myself. It doubles as an off-hand shield.
Stone forgets nothing, but it can be persuaded to keep quiet.

companions.name: Veyra Ashhorn
companions.description: A tiefling contract-breaker healing people harmed by bargains they never understood.
dialogue: Every contract has a door. Most are hidden in the punctuation.
Yes, the horns are real. No, they do not predict weather.
Pell labels poisons with skulls. He labels soup with two skulls.
I charge demons double. Professional discourtesy.
A curse is just a rule with theatrical lighting.
My tail knocked over that bottle. We have discussed boundaries.
I left the Ash Court with one coat and several enemies. Good coat.
Mercy and loopholes are cousins. I am fond of both.

companions.name: Rhazek Dawnscale
companions.description: A dragonkin oath-bearer descended from the guardians who first sealed the Obsidian Gate.
dialogue: My ancestors guarded the gate. They neglected to explain from which side.
I breathe smoke when embarrassed. This is not an invitation to test it.
Cael cheats at cards by being lucky with confidence.
The oath is older than my name and considerably less practical.
Cold mornings make my scales squeak. Speak of this and perish.
A dragonkin bow is mostly horns and apologies.
I keep one sun fragment as a night-light. It is excessive.
Duty should be carried like a spear, not worn like a chain.

companions.name: Gruk Ironjaw
companions.description: An orcish warrior seeking honourable combat to repay a blood debt.
dialogue: Gruk fights. Gruk wins. Gruk eats.
Honour is not spoken. It is done.
Your enemies will know my name before they know the ground.
In my clan, we settle arguments with axes. Efficient.
Small friend, big heart. This I respect.
My jaw is iron. My cooking is questionable.
Orcs do not retreat. We advance in the opposite direction.

companions.name: Pip Sprocket
companions.description: A gnome artificer whose inventions work approximately 60% of the time.
dialogue: Stand back. This might explode. Actually, stand further back.
I call this invention 'The Problem Solver'. The problem is usually still there, but on fire.
Gnomes don't fail. We discover unexpected learning opportunities.
My last apprentice was very understanding. About the explosion. Not about the eyebrows.
Have you considered that the door might be locked for a reason? No? Good. Stand back.
I measured twice and cut once. Both measurements were wrong.
Every great invention begins with 'What could possibly go wrong?'

companions.name: Rose Underhill
companions.description: A halfling scout who has never met a locked door or an untried pie she didn't like.
dialogue: Second breakfast was the best invention. Elevenses was a close second.
I'm not hiding. I'm strategically absent.
Locked doors are just suggestions with better hardware.
The best adventures end with a meal. The worst ones don't end at all.
You call it 'breaking in.' I call it 'uninvited visiting.'
Big folk always look up. Never look down. Their mistake.
I once stole a pie from under a sleeping dragon. The pie was excellent.

companions.name: Ember Skysong
companions.description: A fire genasi whose emotions are uncomfortably visible as temperature changes.
dialogue: When I'm angry, things near me tend to catch fire. Fair warning.
My mother was a fire elemental. My father was a very brave bard.
I don't get colds. I get small, controlled infernos.
Emberwatch is the only town where my temperature isn't alarming.
Sorry about the singed eyebrows. Again.
I meditate to stay cool. Literally.
My tea is always the perfect temperature. That's one advantage.

companions.name: Korrath Peaks
companions.description: A goliath warrior who measures all challenges against the mountains of his youth.
dialogue: The mountain does not flinch. Neither do I.
Among goliaths, we keep score. Always.
Your problems are smaller than my mountains. This is encouraging.
I have faced avalanches. Your enemy is less impressive.
Endurance is not about never falling. It is about standing each time.
My name means 'summit' in the old tongue. I try to live up to it.
Goliath cooking has two spices: rock and more rock.

companions.name: Sythia Coils
companions.description: A naga lamia scholar studying the boundary between mortal and divine magic.
dialogue: My coils are quite comfortable, thank you for not staring.
I have studied for three centuries. I still feel behind.
The divine and the arcane are siblings who refuse to speak.
Yes, I can constrict you. No, that is not an invitation.
Warm-blooded folk are so impatient. I blame the mortality.
I shed my skin once a year. It is less dramatic than it sounds.
My library has books older than your kingdom's founding.

companions.name: Nethys Websong
companions.description: A weaver arachne whose silk traps have stopped entire warbands.
dialogue: Eight legs, eight perspectives. It is quite useful, actually.
My silk is stronger than steel and softer than moonlight.
Do not fear the web. Fear what built it.
I find the assumption that I eat mates both rude and inaccurate.
My grandmother could weave a tapestry that predicted the future.
Surface folk always look at my legs first. Then my eyes. Eventually.
I do not trap my friends. Only my enemies. And the occasional rabbit.
